prompts.core:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: production 2D videogame pixel-art animation sprite sheet, CORE board, 4 columns by 4 rows.
Primary request: Faithful original fan-made pixel-art CHRYSALIS, the AI aerial boss from Metal Gear Solid Peace Walker (1974 design), not a generic aircraft. This must contain 16 separately drawn successive animation poses of THE SAME machine, not one still repeated.
Reference-informed identity: the official Konami / Square Enix Play Arts Kai Chrysalis has a low elongated dark grey angular fuselage, an orange wedge-shaped FRONT nose, TWO LARGE broad flat circular lift discs on lateral articulated pylons and ONE SMALLER circular disc on the slender rear boom, exactly THREE discs in total. Pale small rectangular markings on the discs. A small cylindrical dark AI pod hangs down beneath the orange nose. A very long narrow double-edged rectangular railgun on a mechanical mount hangs underneath the center and points forward. Subtle orange accents, steel joints, near-white circular radome by the lower weapon assembly. NO cockpit glazing, NO pilot, NO legs or wheels, NO conventional helicopter blades. Match these iconic components with careful consistent proportions in every cell.
View: locked orthographic SIDE VIEW, front orange nose and long railgun ALWAYS point RIGHT, rear small disc points LEFT. Slightly elevated side angle only enough to see top surfaces of the discs as broad shallow ellipses; do not switch angles across frames. The near large disc may partly overlap the far large disc but both remain identifiable. Full machine plus its three discs and full gun fit in each cell. Clean crisp pixel clusters, retro high-detail 2D action-game sprite art, restrained grey steel/orange/ivory palette. No painterly blur, no photoreal toy, no display stand.
Scene/backdrop: completely solid exact MAGENTA RGB255,0,255 behind every sprite, no shadows on the backdrop. Exact CYAN RGB0,255,255 thin grid guides: FIVE uninterrupted vertical lines including both outside borders, FIVE horizontal lines including both outside borders, making precisely sixteen equal square cells. No additional marks or text. Output square, grid covers the whole canvas.
Composition calibration: identical apparent machine size in ALL 16 cells. Largest horizontal span NO MORE THAN 60 percent of cell width, maximum height about 42 percent, generous empty margins at least 55 source pixels between every sprite pixel/effect and a guide. Stable center of main hull near center of cell, stable hover height, no cropping, no crossing grid boundaries.
Row 1 = IDLE: four hover stabilization phases, slight alternating rotor-disc pitch and engine-pylon micro-adjustments, railgun at rest forward. Still clearly flying, never standing.
Row 2 = MOVE: four distinct forward-flight thrust phases with subtle nose-down pitch, articulated lift discs changing pitch and rear stabilizer adjustments. Preserve scale and angle; no speed trails.
Row 3 = CHARGE: four successive railgun aim/windup poses: lower mount levels, barrel settles forward, small white-blue energy at muzzle builds subtly; no discharge yet and no beam crossing cell.
Row 4 = ATTACK: four actual railgun firing/recoil/re-settle phases, restrained short white-blue muzzle impulse confined next to the barrel, distinct mechanical mount recoil and discs compensating. Keep the entire machine visible in all four phases.
Constraints: sixteen complete isolated sprites, no labels, no letters, no UI, no watermark, no logos, no scenery, no other characters, no rockets substituted for the railgun, no Rex/Zeke/Shagohod parts. Final sheet ready for automatic grid extraction.
Additional strict fidelity and extraction requirements: keep every sprite SMALL within its cell with large empty margins on all sides; the longest full rear-to-muzzle span occupies only sixty percent of each cell. Main lift discs are very THIN, WIDE saucers, not thick hockey pucks. Two large discs are LATERAL, each mounted on a side pylon, projected partly overlapping in this fixed right-facing side view; rear small disc on a tail boom. The AI pod below the nose must be a clearly visible LONG VERTICAL DARK CYLINDER with an orange bottom rim, NOT a sphere, tyre or wheel. Orange nose is a SHORT BLUNT polygonal wedge, not a long pointed jet beak. Railgun is long rectangular open-truss mechanical barrel, lower than the hull, pointing RIGHT. Short muzzle flash stays fully inside the sprite's safe margin and occupies less than ten percent of cell width. Render no text-like labels on any disc.
prompts.special:
IMPORTANT: THE LONG VENTRAL RAILGUN MUST BE VISIBLE IN EVERY POSE, ESPECIALLY EVERY BOTTOM ROW SCAN FRAME. THREE SOLID SAUCER-LIKE LIFT DISCS, NEVER A LOOP TAIL ROTOR.

Original sprites, not a copy of product photography. Do not make the body a helicopter cabin or add landing feet. Fixed side-view camera and equal size across all 16 cells.

First special: railgun missing from scan row.
Second special: rear disc drifted to a loop-shaped tail rotor and main discs too narrow.

review.identity: Three saucer-like lift discs, low dark-grey hull, orange front nose, suspended AI cylinder, lower pale radome and forward rectangular railgun; right-facing airborne silhouette.
review.actions: Core idle/move/charge/attack; special recover/hit/death/scan; four independently generated phases per state.
review.validation: Strict importer PASS: 32 nonempty authored poses, 8 actions. Runtime cells: 16 distinct image hashes per sheet; minimum alpha-to-frame margin 16 pixels. Final special sheet visually inspected.
review.fidelityLimit: Original fan-made side-view pixel adaptation, not a 1:1 official model or complete canonical moveset. Panel contours and apparent railgun length vary slightly between the two authored boards; no reference photograph or official game pixels included.

calibration.method: One uniform scale applied to all 16 special source cells, anchored by core idle and special scan. No per-pose deformation or synthesis.
